name: Tenstorrent Wormhole Tensix (n150 / n300)
memory_bandwidth_basis: Derived and confirmed by the vendor table: 12 GB GDDR6 on a 192-bit bus at 12 GT/sec = 288 GB/s. The vendor states 288 GB/s directly for n150 and 576 GB/s for n300 (two ASICs), so this is not an independent derivation.
notes: Per n150 card (1 Wormhole ASIC, 72 enabled Tensix cores of 80 built, 108 MB SRAM, 12 GB GDDR6, 160 W, PCIe 4.0 x16). The BF16 row is the same number as FP16 because the vendor's precision table lists BFLOAT16 alongside FP16 without a separate throughput figure; flagged vendor_claim false for that reason. n300 is the same silicon doubled: 2 ASICs, 128 Tensix cores, 192 MB SRAM, 24 GB GDDR6, 576 GB/s, 131 TFLOPS FP16 / 466 FP8, 300 W. ARCHITECTURAL POINT: Wormhole is a small-SRAM, modest-bandwidth design (288 GB/s is roughly a fifth of an H100's) with 108 MB of on-die SRAM acting as a L2-like feed tier, and the architecture pushes data movement onto a network-on-chip with dedicated RISC-V control cores rather than relying on caches. For inference that means it is decisively bandwidth-bound at batch 1 (257 FLOP/byte FP16 does not save it; 288 GB/s is the wall) and the design bets on very low power and open-source software rather than on winning the bandwidth race. Precision support is unusually broad for an inference part: FP8/FP16/BF16, BLOCKFP2/BLOCKFP4/BLOCKFP8, INT8/INT32, UINT8, TF32 - the block-float formats are the ones with native hardware paths. Scale-up is 2x QSFP-DD 200G plus Warp 100 in-card bridges, daisy-chaining into Galaxy racks. Consumer: the n150 is sold as a retail developer card at ~USD 1000-1100, so while it is not a consumer GPU it is sold into the desktop channel. OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE STACK: Tenstorrent's software stack is fully open-source (GitHub: tenstorrent/tt-metal, tenstorrent/tt-forge). TT-Forge is the top-level MLIR-based compiler connecting to OpenXLA, MLIR, ONNX, TVM, PyTorch, and TensorFlow. TT-NN is the operator library. TT-Metalium is the low-level kernel programming model. 800+ model variants tested in CI. This is a key differentiator: unlike proprietary stacks (CUDA, ROCm), the entire stack is auditable and modifiable.
